basis: H3: For the Gromov-Witten classes defined by the cited global Kuranishi construction, prove the complete Kontsevich-Manin CohFT axioms. Given existence/equivalence of global charts, Thom and Gysin facts, the remaining geometric work compares charts under forgetful and nodal clutching maps, factors the non-cartesian clutching diagram through a degree-one birational map on quotient presentations, and establishes the matching exceptional-pushforward/virtual-class relations including nonseparating genus reduction and orbifold intersections. This is one complete CohFT framework; individual axioms, standard descendants and technical chart lemmas are not independent new counts.

H3: Equivariant virtual localisation and the explicit all-genus Gromov-Witten decorated-graph formula for Hamiltonian GKM manifolds. Given the cited global charts and ordinary torus localisation, the author constructs compatible equivariant charts/fixed suborbifolds and identifies their moving obstruction/normal pieces. An intermediate chart with constrained domain topology separates map and domain deformations; graph automorphism quotients, normalised component sequences, moving automorphisms and node-smoothing factors yield the actual Euler-class ratio and graph weights. Ordinary localisation alone does not compute this ratio. Count general virtual localisation with its complete GKM computation and immediate graph-determination/toric corollaries as one author framework, not a problem per graph factor.

H2: Compare global-Kuranishi Gromov-Witten classes with Ruan-Tian pseudocycle classes for semipositive targets. Given the earlier chart construction, general compactness/gluing and cobordism facts, the author still constructs a parameterised perturbed chart over a good finite cover with perturbations supported away from nodes, identifies both endpoint virtual classes with the correct covering degree, and identifies the terminal transverse virtual class with the pseudocycle homology class by the compact-support/Borel-Moore comparison diagram. Stable range is handled geometrically and unstable range by the original Divisor/Symmetry definitions. This is not a mere renaming of the two invariant definitions.
